newsitem.title: EGYPT: Angry Arab ministers say cut ties with Israel.
newsitem.headline: Angry Arab ministers say cut ties with Israel.

text.p: Arab foreign ministers frustrated with Israeli policies took what some of them called their most decisive concerted action against the current government when they recommended suspending normal ties with the Jewish state.
They formally approved on Monday a resolution recommending an end to normal relations with Israel and restoring the economic boycott.
Arab League Secretary General Esmat Abdel-Meguid read out the resolution after the foreign ministers ended two days of talks dominated by Israel's attitude to Middle East peace.
"The Arab League recommended this and this is binding. All members are obliged to stick to the resolution," he added.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu accused Arab states of ganging up on Israel but called the notion that they could revive the Arab boycott "absurd".
Some ministers had described the resolutions drawn up at the Arab League meeting in Cairo as the most decisive concerted action the Arabs have taken since Netanyahu took power last June.

Arab countries have criticised what they see as Netanyahu's brushing aside of agreements between the Palestinians and the government of his predecessor and the land-for-peace principle of peace negotiations.

The crisis in Arab-Israeli relations recently came to a head when Israeli bulldozers broke ground at a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem on March 18 and after an attack days later by a Palestinian suicide bomber in Tel Aviv which killed three Israeli women.
Israel on Monday flattened the bomber's West Bank home in a move assailed by human rights activists as collective punishment.

In a 12th straight day of West Bank violence spurred by the settlement building, Israeli troops firing rubber bullets shot and wounded two Palestinians during a clash near Jenin with about 200 stone-throwing protesters.

The Palestinian Health Ministry said that as of Sunday night Israel had killed one Palestinian, wounded 14 with live bullets and 195 with rubber bullets, and caused 298 to be treated for inhalation of teargas.

The United States, which is the main power broker in the peace talks between Palestinians and the Israelis, tried again to get the two sides to resolve their stalemate, sending U.S. envoy Dennis Ross to the region late last week.
Ross met Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in Morocco and Netanyahu in Jerusalem.
Senior Palestinian security official Colonel Jibril Rajoub said on Monday that the Palestinian Authority has rejected the U.S. initiative to restore security coordination with Israel.
He said that security coordination ended when Netanyahu sent bulldozers to break ground for the new settlement.
Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara told reporters that peace could not be achieved unless Arab land is returned.

"The resolution is very wise because it is aimed at saving the peace process and affirms the commitment of Arabs to peace. It says that peace cannot be achieved unless occupied Arab land is returned," he said.
"Netanyahu's policies have forced Arab countries to take such a decision. Arabs have taken a wise decision in response to a clumsy and stupid policy," Shara said
The effect will be somewhat diluted because those with formal agreements with Israel -- Egypt, Jordan and the Palestinians -- are not required to enforce them.
Netanyahu said on Monday Arabs should not revert to threats whenever their relations with Israel were strained.

"What is required on the Arab side is to recognise that we are not always going to have agreement with Israel but that we don't go back to this mode of 'ganging up' on Israel and making these absurd ideas that the boycott will be reinstated," Netanyahu told Israel Radio's English news.
"Israel has known periods of Israel-bashing more than once and we've been able to overcome it," he said.
Farouk Kaddoumi, the hardline head of the PLO's political (foreign affairs) department, said the Israel premier was trying to wipe out Palestinians.

"Netanyahu should go to hell. I've said it several times. He is a hardliner. He thinks we (Palestinans) are Red Indians. I respect Red Indians. He comes from Brooklyn, from the United States. He thinks he can annihilate the Palestinians. Netanyahu is like Hitler."

The decision to halt steps towards normalisation with Israel was hailed as a victory by Syria and Lebanon, which have long urged other Arab states such as Oman, Qatar, Morocco and Tunisia not to rush towards creating ties with the Jewish state.
